chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Humayri quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, on the authority of Abi Wilad (al-Hannat), on the authority of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) said: 'Indeed, the knowledge/perception of the perfection of a Muslim's faith is his leaving off speech in what does not concern him, and his quarreling rarely, his forbearance, his patience, and his good character.'
ai.seo_question: What are the five signs of a perfected Muslim faith according to Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS) links the perfection of faith to social and ethical conduct, emphasizing that true knowledge manifests in restraint from idle speculation and conflict. This teaching reflects the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and *hilm* (forbearance) as practical markers of spiritual maturity, aligning with the broader tradition of the Ahl al-Bayt regarding the integration of inner belief and outer behavior.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 5-51 Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Abdullah ibn Ja’far al-Homayry quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Mahboob, on the authority of Abi Vilad (al-Hinat), on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) that Ali ibn al-Hussein as-Sajjad (MGB) said, “Indeed the perfection of a Muslim’s faith can be recognized by the following five things: not saying absurd things; quarrelling rarely; having perseverance; being patient and being good-tempered.”
